content.thinking:
I'm diagnosing the issue: browser steering worked fine across logins, cookie walls, retries, and captchas, each action taking a few seconds, but I found one real bug where an empty `lines` list was wrongly treated as a zero-position bid (now fixed), plus some sloppy handling in how facts get saved and passed.

Qwen itself isn't the weak link — it successfully cleared every gate, located the right material, and retrieved the TAN, but it's slow and unable to stop early: calls routinely took 90-117 seconds with 5-7K reasoning tokens and 20-27K tokens of context, and it ended up revisiting the same viewer URL ~15 times, burning through all 80 turns, with long stretches of almost no browser activity while it just thought. Across 293 total calls there were roughly 3 calls running in parallel at any given time, but the bigger structural problem is the pipeline itself running strictly sequentially (research, then analyst, then submit) despite rules allowing parallel site access, so ERP didn't even start until 9:45 and the run never got submitted for scoring. I also note that quality dominates the scoring formula, with cost and time only breaking ties — the current leader sits at quality 21.5, $0.38, and 16 minutes.

Given the heavy reasoning this pricing task requires, model intelligence really does drive quality. On OpenRouter, Qwen's cheap per-token pricing (~$0.15/$0.47 per M) kept run #1 around $0.30 despite using ~6M input tokens, whereas a frontier model like Sonnet would likely cost $15+ for similar volume — but since cost only matters as a tiebreaker, that tradeoff is secondary to raw quality. The bigger concern is latency from the Atira-hosted Qwen's queue waits, which in run #2 totaled nearly 11 minutes across 155 calls (p95 14s), eating up close to half of total call time — that's a real infrastructure cost independent of the model's own speed, and it's unclear why queueing is so heavy when the team's concurrency limit shouldn't be binding.

My recommendation: go hybrid — use a strong frontier model for the actual pricing/analyst reasoning (just a couple of calls with small inputs, so cost stays low) since quality dominates there, while keeping Qwen for cheap bulk browsing work, possibly with its thinking mode disabled during navigation steps to cut latency (though I should flag that toggle is unverified via the proxy). The other major lever is running all four research agents in parallel from the start with capped context and clear stop conditions. I'll note that run #2 is still in progress so I shouldn't predict its outcome, and that Qwen costs are simulated/free for the user while OpenRouter usage is real money — worth calling out explicitly, and I'll keep the explanation concise.

content.text:
**Short answer: mostly none of the three.** The browser steering works and the JSON had one bug that's already fixed. Qwen isn't dumb, but it's slow and doesn't know when to stop. And the pipeline makes that worse by running steps one after another that could run in parallel. This is based on the logs of sandbox run #1 (`run_71d7ac1e0e08a1c0`).

**Browser steering works.** Qwen got through the logins, cookie walls, the 503 retry, the slider and "Ich bin kein Roboter" gates and the Empfangsnummer form. It found ERP material HZ-8405 through catalogue group GR-8923, and the submit agent found the signing TAN in the mail. Each browser action takes 3–5 seconds. Nothing is stuck on the browser side.

**The JSON contract had one real bug.** An empty `lines` list was read as a "bid", so it produced a bid with 0 positions. That's fixed. There's also some sloppiness, like `save_fact {"facts": "{}"}` and facts passed as a string instead of an object. Neither caused the timeout.

**Qwen is capable, but overthinks and doesn't stop:**
- Between minutes 4 and 9 the browsers barely moved because the model was thinking. Single calls took 90–117 seconds and wrote 5–7K output tokens each.
- Each call carries 20–27K tokens of context. The spec agent used 1.7M prompt tokens over 80 calls.
- The spec agent opened the same viewer URL about 15 times and used all 80 turns, although its facts were complete much earlier.
- The mail agent's last model call timed out at 12:01.

**The pipeline is the real problem:**
- The ERP agent only started at 9:45 and got about 2 minutes, because it waited for the spec agent. The rules say sites can be worked in parallel with no fixed order.
- Research, then analyst, then submit run strictly in sequence. The submit agent had the TAN at 18:58, exactly when the deadline hit. The run never submitted, so it has no score.
- In run #2, which is still going, Atira's Qwen added **10:54 of queue wait** across 155 calls (p95 14 s). That's slowness from the hosting, not from the model.

## Why Qwen vs. OpenRouter

You're allowed to use OpenRouter: the rules accept your own key and meter the calls at published prices. But look at how ranking works: **eligible first, then quality, and cost × time only decides between equal quality.** The leader has quality 21.5 at $0.38 and 16 minutes. Right now quality is what counts, and speed and spend barely matter.

That argues for a **hybrid**, not swapping everything:
- **Use a frontier model for the analyst / pricing step.** Rules 12–28 are a heavy pricing calculation where model quality decides the score. It's only one or two calls with a few thousand tokens of facts, so it costs cents.
- **Think twice before moving browsing off Qwen.** Run #1 used about 6M input tokens. At Qwen's simulated $0.15/M that cost $0.30. At Sonnet-class prices it would be roughly $15+ for the same run (less with caching), and that's real money from your key, while Qwen is free to you. A faster model could be worth it if it cuts turns and queue wait. But the cheaper fixes are the ones above:
  - start all 4 research agents at t=0
  - trim tool results
  - stop agents once their required facts are saved
  - limit Qwen's thinking on navigation steps (I haven't checked whether Atira's proxy lets you turn that down)

A sensible next step: once run #2 finishes, compare it with run #1. Then try the analyst on Claude or GPT through OpenRouter while browsing stays on Qwen. That isolates whether the model is what limits quality.

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

lastPrompt: So would my claude oauth key also work

content.content:
**Anthropic authentication through the proxy:** Anthropic calls use the base URL `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic`, which forwards to api.anthropic.com. The proxy passes your key through unchanged. The doc says to "Send your provider key the way the provider expects it: `x-api-key` (Anthropic)." The proxy never stores, logs, or returns the key. With `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` set, the Anthropic SDK needs no other changes: it reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and sends it as `x-api-key`. A request without its own key gets a `401` unless the organizers pay for that provider, in which case the proxy adds their key to the run's calls.

**Accepted key types:** The doc doesn't say. It refers only to "your own key" or "your provider key" and gives header formats, not key categories. It doesn't mention OAuth tokens or Claude subscriptions, so I can't confirm either is accepted.

**Where team secrets go:** Team secrets are environment variables for your agent's run step in test and scored runs, such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`. You can manage them on the team page under Secrets, or with your personal token via the API. The doc says that "For test and scored runs, keep it as a team secret, not in your package," because packages are stored and the review agent reads them. Values are encrypted, never shown again, and redacted from run logs. Setup never receives them.

content.text:
You have a custom harness because of one decision the thread made at 12:06: **use Atira's free Qwen.** Claude Code only speaks Anthropic's API, so running it on Qwen would need a translation proxy in the sandbox. That's an extra part that can break, so the thread wrote a small loop instead. The original goal was actually "Qwen with Claude Code as harness"; it moved to the custom loop after you said "take the harness that works best". If you're willing to use Claude as the model, that reason goes away.

Whichever you pick, the browser side is the same. The harness talks to Playwright MCP, and Playwright MCP connects to the sandbox browsers over CDP (`CDP_URLS`). Only the loop around it changes: who calls the model, keeps the context, decides when to stop and enforces the deadline.

## The options

| | Harness | Model | Billing | Main catch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Custom loop (now)** | your Python loop | Qwen | free, cheap simulated cost | you maintain the loop. Its context handling is basic, which is part of why calls are 20–27K tokens and agents don't stop |
| **B. Claude Code CLI** | `claude -p` per site, Playwright MCP on that site's CDP | Claude | subscription or API key | deadlines are coarse (`--max-turns`, kill the process). Subscription use in an automated run is a grey area, and the proxy pass-through is untested |
| **C. Claude Code + Qwen** | `claude -p` | Qwen through a translation proxy (e.g. LiteLLM) | free | extra moving part. Claude Code's prompts are tuned for Claude, so Qwen may do worse in it |
| **D. Claude Agent SDK** | Claude Code's loop as a Python library inside `agent.py` | Claude | API key only (the terms don't allow subscription tokens with the SDK) | costs real money |

## Recommendation

**D (Agent SDK with an API key) is the strongest setup.** You get Claude Code's harness: tool use, context compaction and a model that knows when it's done. You also keep what your loop does well, because orchestration stays in Python:
- run 4 site agents in parallel with hard deadlines
- `save_facts` as a tool inside your own code
- structured output for the analyst

It removes the two biggest problems in run #1: Qwen's 100-second thinking calls and Atira's Qwen queue wait (10:54 in run #2).

**B is the only option that can use your subscription.** It needs a test run to find out whether Atira's proxy passes the subscription token through. It also gives you less control over timing.

**The trade-off is cost.** A Claude run will clearly cost more than Qwen's $0.30. But ranking is quality first, and cost × time only decides between equal quality. With the leader at quality 21.5, a working, accurate bid matters far more.

The cheapest way to decide is to port one site agent (tender or spec) to D, run it locally against the scouting sites, and compare turns, time and facts with Qwen's run on the same site. Want me to do that? It needs an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in your environment. Or, if you'd rather try your subscription, I'll run the B test from my last message first.

content.thinking:
I'm weighing the advantages of a custom harness over Claude Code: freedom to pick cheaper models like Qwen, tighter time control with per-agent deadlines and cancellation, and finer control over what context gets passed into each turn.

On the Claude Code side, its system prompt and built-in tools (Bash, Read, Edit) add fixed token overhead and introduce risk — unrestricted Bash could end up writing a crawler mid-run, which might brush against fair-play rules against autonomous discovery, though restricting tools with --allowedTools could mitigate that. A custom harness also offers cleaner setup with no npm install or login steps, plus more transparent, structured data handoff through explicit required-key checks and stop hints rather than relying on MCP or the Agent SDK.

But the downside is real: building your own loop means reimplementing things Claude Code already handles well — compaction, retries, parallel tool calls, mature prompting — and the earlier run already exposed where a custom loop falls short. Ultimately the harness decision mostly follows from the model choice: Qwen pushes toward a custom harness, while Claude makes the Agent SDK attractive since it preserves Claude Code's loop while still giving control — leaving token overhead and full customization as the only real argument left for going fully custom with Claude.

content.text:
The real advantage is **model choice**. Most of the others you can also get from the Claude Agent SDK.

**What your own harness gives you:**

1. **Any model, including the free one.** Your loop runs on Atira's Qwen (simulated $0.15/$0.47 per M tokens, free to you), and it could use Clef for quick yes/no decisions. Claude Code natively only speaks Anthropic's API, so using Qwen there means adding a translation proxy.
2. **Hard control of time.** With a 20-minute limit, the harness has to guarantee that submit gets its slot. Your loop can cut off any agent or model call at a deadline it computes. With the Claude Code CLI you only get `--max-turns` or killing the process.
3. **Control of every token in the context.** You decide what goes into each call: trimmed snapshots, dropped old tool results, only the brief section an agent needs. Claude Code adds its own system prompt and built-in tool definitions to every call, and that overhead counts in your cost score. Your loop isn't using this control well yet; that's why calls are 20–27K tokens.
4. **Easier fair-play review.** The rules forbid crawlers and fixed scripts, and a reviewer reads your package. A small loop whose only tools are browser actions plus `save_facts` is clearly "model decides". Claude Code comes with Bash, and mid-run it might write a script that crawls the sites. You'd have to restrict its tools (`--allowedTools`) to stay safe.
5. **Fewer moving parts in the sandbox.** There's no npm CLI to install and no login to carry into the run.

**What Claude Code gives you instead:**
- a mature loop with context compaction and retries
- a model that's good at knowing when it's done
- reliable tool use

Run #1 showed the weak spots of your loop in exactly those areas: agents that don't stop, and growing context.

**Bottom line:** the harness choice follows from the model choice.
- **Staying on Qwen:** keep your own harness. Claude Code on Qwen adds a proxy and gives up its main strength, which is Claude.
- **Moving to Claude:** use the **Agent SDK**. It gives you Claude Code's loop, and you keep points 2, 4 and 5: Python orchestration and deadlines, your own tools, and only the tools you allow. You lose only some of point 3, the per-call overhead.

content.text:
Yes. The Agent SDK is the programming interface to Claude Code; it isn't a separate engine. The Python package (`claude-agent-sdk`) starts the Claude Code CLI as a subprocess and talks to it over a JSON stream. So the agent loop, tool calling, context compaction and Playwright MCP support are the same code that `claude -p` runs.

**What the SDK adds on top:**
- **Control from Python.** You drive sessions with `query()` or `ClaudeSDKClient`, can run several in parallel with `asyncio`, and can cancel one at a deadline.
- **Your own tools in-process.** `save_facts` could be a plain Python function registered as an in-process MCP tool, with no separate server.
- **Hooks.** You can inspect or block a tool call before it runs, or react after it. For example: refuse `Bash`, or tell the agent "required facts complete, finish now".
- **Configuration per session.** You set the allowed tools, the Playwright MCP server for that site's CDP URL, max turns and the model.
- **A lighter default system prompt.** I believe the SDK uses a minimal system prompt unless you choose the `claude_code` preset, which would cut some per-call overhead. I haven't verified that for the current version. You'd still restrict the built-in tools (`Bash`, `Read`, and so on) yourself.

**What it means for you:**
- **Auth:** an API key only. Anthropic's terms don't allow subscription tokens with the SDK. Only the plain `claude` CLI may use your subscription.
- **Sandbox:** because it runs the Claude Code binary underneath, `setup` has to install it. I believe recent Python SDK versions bundle the CLI, so `uv sync` might be enough. Otherwise it's an `npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` in setup. I'd check this in the first test run.
- **Network:** model calls go out through `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, which the sandbox already points at Atira's proxy. The proxy meters them.

So "Agent SDK vs. Claude Code" isn't really a choice of harness. It's the same harness, either scripted from your Python orchestrator (SDK) or launched as a CLI process (`claude -p`).

content.text:
**For speed and cost, a custom harness wins.** opencode and Claude Code are built for coding, and that design costs you on every call.

**Why the custom harness is better here:**
- **Cost is tokens × price.** A coding harness sends its long system prompt and a dozen tool definitions (file edit, shell, search and so on) with every call. That's several thousand tokens you don't need, multiplied by about 300 calls per run. Your loop can send a short prompt with only browser tools plus `save_facts`.
- **Time is turns × latency.** The biggest savings come from how the run is organized, and a generic harness doesn't let you control that: parallel agents from t=0, a hard deadline per phase, a forced stop once the required facts are saved, and trimming old snapshots from the context.
- **Model choice is already solved.** Qwen at $0.15/$0.47 per M tokens is about as cheap as it gets. opencode does support OpenAI-compatible models natively, so unlike Claude Code it could run Qwen without a translation proxy. But it still brings the coding overhead and gives you less control, so it doesn't beat your loop.

**Where the time actually goes (from run #1), and the fixes in order of impact:**
1. **Start all 4 research agents at t=0.** The ERP agent waited until 9:45 and got only 2 minutes.
2. **Make each turn's context smaller.** Cap snapshot and `evaluate` output, and drop old snapshots from history. Right now calls are about 21K tokens each (1.7M over 80 calls).
3. **Force a finish once required facts are saved.** The spec agent had its facts around turn 30 and ran 50 more turns.
4. **Reduce Qwen's thinking on navigation steps.** Several calls took 90–117 s and wrote 5–7K output tokens. I'd have to check whether Atira's proxy lets you turn thinking down (e.g. `enable_thinking: false`).
5. **Use helpers that extract a page the model picked.** The rules allow that, and it saves several turns per page.
6. **Use a stronger model only where quality needs it**, probably the analyst. That's one call, so it barely moves cost × time.

**Remember the order of the ranking:** quality first, and cost × time only decides between equal quality. A fast, cheap run with a wrong bid loses to a slow, correct one. So keep the Claude experiment in mind as a quality check — does Claude find facts Qwen misses? — but not as the way to pick the harness.

The other thread is still working in `my-agent/`, so these fixes should go there rather than to a second agent working in parallel. Fixes 1–3 are partly underway already. Fix 4 is the open question I can check quickly if you want.

70	class Agent:
71	    """One model session with tools over named browsers. Use `async with Agent(...) as agent: await agent.run(...)`."""
72	
73	    def __init__(self, name: str, browsers: dict[str, str], workdir: Path, model: str = "qwen"):
74	        self.name, self.browsers, self.model = name, browsers, model
75	        self.dir = workdir / name
76	        self.downloads = self.dir / "downloads"
77	        self.downloads.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
78	        self.facts_path = self.dir / "facts.json"
79	        self.log = (self.dir / "transcript.jsonl").open("w")
80	        self.sessions: dict[str, ClientSession] = {}
81	        self.tools: list[dict] = []
82	        self.client = qwen_client()
83	        self.facts = None
84	        self.finished = None
85	        self.required: list[str] = []
86	        self.usage = {"calls": 0, "prompt_tokens": 0, "completion_tokens": 0}
87	        self._stack = AsyncExitStack()
88	
89	    async def __aenter__(self):
90	        try:
91	            for browser, cdp_url in self.browsers.items():
92	                params = StdioServerParameters(command=str(PLAYWRIGHT_MCP), cwd=str(self.dir), args=[
93	                    "--cdp-endpoint", cdp_url, "--output-dir", str(self.downloads), "--image-responses", "omit",
94	                    "--timeout-action", "10000"])
95	                read, write = await self._stack.enter_async_context(stdio_client(params))
96	                session = await self._stack.enter_async_context(ClientSession(read, write))
97	                await asyncio.wait_for(session.initialize(), 60)
98	                self.sessions[browser] = session
99	                for tool in (await asyncio.wait_for(session.list_tools(), 60)).tools:
100	                    if tool.name in BROWSER_TOOLS:
101	                        self.tools.append(_openai_tool(f"{browser}__{tool.name}", tool.description,
102	                                                       tool.input_schema))
103	        except BaseException:
104	            await self.__aexit__()
105	            raise
106	        self.tools += LOCAL_TOOLS
107	        return self
108	
109	    async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
110	        self.log.close()
111	        await self._stack.aclose()
112	
113	    def _print(self, text: str):
114	        print(f"[{self.name}] {text}", flush=True)
115	
116	    async def run(self, system: str, task: str, deadline: float, max_turns: int = 80,
117	                  required: list[str] | None = None, progress_checks: bool = True) -> dict:
118	        """Loop until the model calls finish, the turns run out or `deadline` (time.monotonic()) passes.
119	        `required`: top-level keys the saved facts must have; the model is reminded of missing ones and cannot
120	        finish without them (unless time runs out)."""
121	        self.required = required or []
122	        messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": task}]
123	        started, nudged = time.monotonic(), False
124	        for turn in range(max_turns):
125	            left = deadline - time.monotonic()
126	            if left < 5:
127	                self._print("deadline reached")
128	                break
129	            if left < 60 and not nudged:
130	                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Less than a minute left: save_facts with everything you "
131	                                 "have now, then finish."})
132	                nudged = True
133	            if progress_checks and turn and turn % 10 == 0:
134	                missing = missing_keys(self.facts, self.required)
135	                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Progress check: call save_facts now with everything "
136	                                 "you found so far." + (f" Still missing: {', '.join(missing)}." if missing else "")})
137	            _compact(messages)
138	            try:
139	                response = await asyncio.wait_for(self.client.chat.completions.create(
140	                    model=self.model, messages=messages, tools=self.tools, temperature=0.2), timeout=min(left, 300))
141	            except (asyncio.TimeoutError, Exception) as error:  # noqa: BLE001  keep the facts saved so far
142	                self._print(f"model call failed: {error!r}")
143	                break
144	            self._count(response)
145	            message = response.choices[0].message
146	            messages.append(_assistant_message(message))
147	            self.log.write(json.dumps({"turn": turn, "assistant": messages[-1]}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
148	            if not message.tool_calls:
149	                if self.finished is not None:
150	                    break
151	                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Continue with the tools. When you are done, call "
152	                                 "save_facts with everything you found, then finish."})
153	                continue
154	            for call in message.tool_calls:
155	                result = await self._call(call.function.name, call.function.arguments)
156	                self._print(f"{time.monotonic() - started:5.0f}s {call.function.name} {_loggable(call)}")
157	                messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "name": call.function.name,
158	                                 "content": result[:MAX_RESULT_CHARS]})
159	                self.log.write(json.dumps({"turn": turn, "tool": call.function.name, "result": result[:3000]},
160	                                          ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
161	            if self.finished is not None:
162	                break
163	        self.log.flush()
164	        return {"name": self.name, "seconds": round(time.monotonic() - started), "facts": self.facts,
165	                "summary": self.finished, "usage": self.usage}
166	
167	    def _count(self, response):
168	        self.usage["calls"] += 1
169	        if response.usage:
170	            self.usage["prompt_tokens"] += response.usage.prompt_tokens or 0
171	            self.usage["completion_tokens"] += response.usage.completion_tokens or 0
172	
173	    async def _call(self, name: str, arguments: str) -> str:
174	        try:
175	            args = json.loads(arguments or "{}")
176	        except ValueError:
177	            return f"Error: the arguments are not valid JSON: {arguments[:200]}"
178	        if name == "save_facts":
179	            self.facts = args.get("facts", args)
180	            self.facts_path.write_text(json.dumps(self.facts, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
181	            missing = missing_keys(self.facts, self.required)
182	            return "Saved." + (f" Still missing: {', '.join(missing)}." if missing else (
183	                " Everything required is there: finish now, unless a value you know exists is still unread."))
184	        if name == "finish":
185	            missing = missing_keys(self.facts, self.required)
186	            if missing:
187	                return (f"Not finished: the saved facts have no {', '.join(missing)}. Collect them, call "
188	                        "save_facts with the complete JSON, then finish.")
189	            self.finished = args.get("summary", "")
190	            return "Finished."
191	        if name == "read_file":
192	            return self._read_file(args.get("name", ""))
193	        browser, _, tool = name.partition("__")
194	        session = self.sessions.get(browser)
195	        if session is None or tool not in BROWSER_TOOLS:
196	            return f"Error: unknown tool {name}"
197	        try:
198	            result = await asyncio.wait_for(session.call_tool(tool, args), timeout=90)
199	        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001  the model decides how to recover
200	            return f"Error: {error!r}"
201	        text = "\n".join(getattr(part, "text", "") for part in result.content if getattr(part, "type", "") == "text")
202	        return self._inline_files(text) or "(no text result)"
203	
204	    def _inline_files(self, text: str) -> str:
205	        """Playwright MCP sometimes links a snapshot file instead of including it: put the page into the result."""
206	        def inline(match):
207	            path = Path(match.group(1))
208	            path = path if path.is_absolute() else self.dir / path
209	            try:
210	                return "```yaml\n" + path.read_text()[:MAX_RESULT_CHARS] + "\n```"
211	            except OSError:
212	                return match.group(0)
213	        return SNAPSHOT_LINK.sub(inline, text)
214	
215	    def _read_file(self, name: str) -> str:
216	        files = sorted(p for p in self.downloads.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
217	        if not name:
218	            return "Downloaded files:\n" + "\n".join(p.name for p in files) if files else "No files downloaded yet."
219	        match = next((p for p in files if p.name == name or str(p).endswith(name)), None)
220	        if match is None:
221	            return f"No downloaded file named {name}. Downloaded: {[p.name for p in files]}"
222	        try:
223	            return read_document(match)
224	        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
225	            return f"Error reading {name}: {error!r}"
226	
227	
228	LOCAL_TOOLS = [
229	    {"type": "function", "function": {
230	        "name": "save_facts",
231	        "description": "Save everything you found so far as one JSON object (replaces the previous save). Save "
232	                       "often, so your work survives if you are stopped.",
233	        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"facts": {"type": "object"}}, "required": ["facts"]}}},
234	    {"type": "function", "function": {
235	        "name": "read_file",
236	        "description": "Read a file the browser downloaded (ZIP, PDF, CSV, text). Without a name, list them.",
237	        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}}}}},
238	    {"type": "function", "function": {
239	        "name": "finish",
240	        "description": "Stop working. Call save_facts first.",
241	        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"summary": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["summary"]}}},
242	]
243	
244	
245	def _loggable(call) -> str:
246	    """A tool call for the log, without what is typed into forms (logins, TANs)."""
247	    if call.function.name.endswith(("browser_fill_form", "browser_type")):
248	        try:
249	            args = json.loads(call.function.arguments or "{}")
250	        except ValueError:
251	            return "(form input)"
252	        fields = args.get("fields") or [args]
253	        return "(form input: " + ", ".join(str(f.get("name") or f.get("element") or "?") for f in fields)[:100] + ")"
254	    return call.function.arguments[:100]
255	
256	
257	def _openai_tool(name: str, description: str | None, schema: dict | None) -> dict:
258	    schema = dict(schema or {"type": "object", "properties": {}})
259	    schema.pop("$schema", None)
260	    return {"type": "function", "function": {"name": name, "description": (description or "")[:1000],
261	                                             "parameters": schema}}
262	
263	
264	def _assistant_message(message) -> dict:
265	    out = {"role": "assistant", "content": message.content or ""}
266	    if message.tool_calls:
267	        out["tool_calls"] = [{"id": c.id, "type": "function",
268	                              "function": {"name": c.function.name, "arguments": c.function.arguments}}
269	                             for c in message.tool_calls]
270	    return out
271	
272	
273	def _compact(messages: list[dict]):
274	    """Old page snapshots dominate the context: keep the latest few whole, shorten the older ones. Results that
275	    carry data the model asked for (evaluate, read_file) stay, so it never has to read a page twice."""
276	    snapshots = [m for m in messages if m["role"] == "tool" and "__browser_" in m.get("name", "")
277	                 and not m["name"].endswith("browser_evaluate") and "```yaml" in m["content"]]
278	    for message in snapshots[:-KEEP_FULL_RESULTS]:
279	        if len(message["content"]) > OLD_RESULT_CHARS:
280	            message["content"] = message["content"][:OLD_RESULT_CHARS] + "\n[... older page snapshot shortened]"
281	
282	
283	def missing_keys(facts, required: list[str]) -> list[str]:
284	    """Required top-level keys that are absent or empty in the saved facts."""
285	    facts = facts if isinstance(facts, dict) else {}
286	    return [key for key in required if facts.get(key) in (None, "", [], {})]

27	PROMPTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "prompts"
28	BROWSERS = ["tender", "spec", "erp", "mail"]           # browser n works on one website
29	SITE_IDS = {"tender": "tender-portal", "spec": "customer-portal", "erp": "erp", "mail": "mail"}
30	REQUIRED = {"tender": ["tender", "positions", "clarifications"], "spec": ["revisions", "requirements"],
31	            "mail": ["mails"], "erp": ["materials"], "submit": ["confirmation"]}
32	ANALYST_S = 120             # the analyst's longest wait
33	SUBMIT_S = 570              # the submit agent: the form, the TAN mail, signing
34	SAFETY_S = 60                # an answer after expires_at scores 0

36	
37	def site(task: dict, site_id: str) -> dict:
38	    found = next(s for s in task["access"] if s.get("siteId") == site_id)
39	    return {"url": found["url"], **(found.get("credentials") or {})}

42	def fill(template: str, **values) -> str:
43	    text = (PROMPTS / template).read_text()
44	    for key, value in values.items():
45	        text = text.replace("{" + key + "}", str(value))

49	def site_task(name: str, task: dict, **extra) -> str:
50	    s = site(task, SITE_IDS[name])
51	    return fill(f"{name}.md", SITE_URL=s["url"], USERNAME=s.get("username", ""), PASSWORD=s.get("password", ""),
52	                BRIEF=task["brief"], **extra)

54	
55	def submission_section(brief: str) -> str:
56	    """The brief's part about entering the bid (from its "Submission" heading); the whole brief if it has none."""
57	    match = re.search(r"^#+ *(Submission|Abgabe|Angebotsabgabe)\b.*$", brief, re.M | re.I)
58	    return brief[match.start():] if match else brief

61	def german(value) -> str:
62	    """1234.5 -> "1.234,50", the format the tender portal expects."""
63	    return f"{Decimal(str(value)):,.2f}".replace(",", "X").replace(".", ",").replace("X", ".")

66	def bid_text(answer: dict) -> str:
67	    lines = [f"Tender reference: {answer['tender_reference']}", f"Decision: {answer['decision']}",
68	             f"Discount: {german(answer['discount_percent'])} %"]
69	    for p in answer["positions"]:
70	        lines.append(f"- Position {p['position']}: material {p['material_number']}, quantity {p['quantity']} Stück, "
71	                     f"unit price {german(p['unit_price'])} EUR, lead time {p['lead_time_weeks']} weeks, "
72	                     f"base unit price {german(p['base_unit_price'])}, surcharge per unit "
73	                     f"{german(p['surcharge_per_unit'])}, packaging per unit {german(p['packaging_per_unit'])}, "
74	                     f"rebate total {german(p['rebate_total'])}")
75	    lines.append(f"Total net: {german(answer['total_net'])} EUR")
76	    return "\n".join(lines)

79	async def research(task: dict, urls: dict, workdir: Path, deadline: float) -> dict:
80	    """Tender, specification and mailbox in parallel; the ERP as soon as the specification agent has saved the
81	    requirements with their catalogue groups. Each site gets its own share of the clock."""
82	    system = (PROMPTS / "system.md").read_text()
83	    agents: dict[str, Agent] = {}
84	    start = time.monotonic()
85	
86	    async def run_site(name: str, prompt: str, until: float) -> dict:
87	        try:
88	            async with Agent(name, {name: urls[name]}, workdir) as agent:
89	                agents[name] = agent
90	                return await agent.run(system, prompt, min(until, deadline), required=REQUIRED[name])
91	        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001  one site failing must not stop the others
92	            print(f"[{name}] failed: {error!r}", flush=True)
93	            return {"name": name, "facts": agents[name].facts if name in agents else None, "error": repr(error)}
94	
95	    share = deadline - start
96	    tender = asyncio.create_task(run_site("tender", site_task("tender", task), start + 0.6 * share))
97	    spec = asyncio.create_task(run_site("spec", site_task("spec", task), start + 0.5 * share))
98	    mail = asyncio.create_task(run_site("mail", site_task("mail", task), start + 0.75 * share))
99	
100	    def facts_of(name: str):
101	        return agents[name].facts if name in agents else None
102	
103	    async def erp_when_requirements_known():
104	        while not spec.done() and time.monotonic() < deadline - 0.4 * share:
105	            f = facts_of("spec")
106	            if isinstance(f, dict) and f.get("requirements") and "atalog" in json.dumps(f, ensure_ascii=False):
107	                break
108	            await asyncio.sleep(5)
109	        print(f"[erp] starting at {time.monotonic() - start:.0f}s", flush=True)
110	        requirements = {"specification": facts_of("spec"), "tender": facts_of("tender")}
111	        return await run_site("erp", site_task("erp", task, REQUIREMENTS=json.dumps(requirements, ensure_ascii=False)),
112	                              deadline)
113	
114	    erp = asyncio.create_task(erp_when_requirements_known())
115	    reports = await asyncio.gather(tender, spec, mail, erp)
116	    for r in reports:
117	        print(f"[{r['name']}] {r.get('seconds')}s, usage {r.get('usage')}, summary: {str(r.get('summary'))[:300]}",
118	              flush=True)
119	    return {r["name"]: r.get("facts") for r in reports}
120	
121	
122	async def submit(task: dict, urls: dict, workdir: Path, answer: dict, deadline: float) -> dict:
123	    t, m = site(task, "tender-portal"), site(task, "mail")
124	    prompt = fill("submit.md", TENDER_URL=t["url"], TENDER_USERNAME=t.get("username", ""),
125	                  TENDER_PASSWORD=t.get("password", ""), MAIL_URL=m["url"], MAIL_USERNAME=m.get("username", ""),
126	                  MAIL_PASSWORD=m.get("password", ""), BRIEF=submission_section(task["brief"]), BID=bid_text(answer))
127	    system = (PROMPTS / "system.md").read_text()
128	    async with Agent("submit", {"tender": urls["tender"], "mail": urls["mail"]}, workdir) as agent:
129	        return await agent.run(system, prompt, deadline, max_turns=120, required=REQUIRED["submit"],
130	                               progress_checks=False)
131	
132	
133	async def solve(task: dict, cdp_urls: list[str]) -> dict | None:
134	    """Research, analyse, price, submit. `task` is the run; `cdp_urls` its browsers, one per website.
135	
136	    The answer goes on the tender portal ("site" submission), so this returns None; it prints the bid."""
137	    start = time.monotonic()
138	    end = start + min(contract.seconds_left(task), 20 * 60) - SAFETY_S
139	    urls = dict(zip(BROWSERS, cdp_urls))
140	    workdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rfq-run-"))
141	    print(f"Workdir {workdir}; {end - start:.0f}s on the clock", flush=True)
142	
143	    facts = await research(task, urls, workdir, deadline=end - SUBMIT_S - ANALYST_S)
144	    (workdir / "facts.json").write_text(json.dumps(facts, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
145	    print(f"Research done at {time.monotonic() - start:.0f}s", flush=True)
146	
147	    try:
148	        decided = await analyst.analyse(task["brief"], facts,
149	                                        timeout=max(60, min(ANALYST_S, end - time.monotonic() - SUBMIT_S)))
150	        (workdir / "order.json").write_text(json.dumps(decided, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
151	        positions = (facts.get("tender") or {}).get("positions") if isinstance(facts.get("tender"), dict) else None
152	        answer = analyst.to_answer(decided, expected_positions=len(positions) if positions else None)
153	    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
154	        print(f"Analysis failed: {error!r}", flush=True)
155	        return None
156	    print(f"Bid at {time.monotonic() - start:.0f}s: {decided.get('decision')} because {decided.get('decision_notes')}",
157	          flush=True)
158	    for line in decided.get("lines") or []:
159	        print(f"  {line.get('position')}: {line.get('quantity_pieces')} pcs, material {line.get('material')} "
160	              f"({str(line.get('material_reasoning'))[:200]})", flush=True)
161	    print(bid_text(answer), flush=True)
162	    (workdir / "bid.json").write_text(json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
163	
164	    report = await submit(task, urls, workdir, answer, deadline=end)
165	    print(f"Submit: {time.monotonic() - start:.0f}s, usage {report.get('usage')}, facts {report.get('facts')}, "
166	          f"summary: {report.get('summary')}", flush=True)
167	    return None
168	
169	
170	async def main() -> int:
171	    task, token = contract.load_run()
172	    sites = ", ".join(f"{s.get('siteId')} {s.get('url')}" for s in task["access"])
173	    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
174	          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
175	    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
176	        cdp_urls, local_browsers = await browsers.cdp_endpoints(playwright, len(BROWSERS))
177	        try:
178	            answer = await solve(task, cdp_urls)
179	        finally:
180	            for browser in local_browsers:
181	                await browser.close()
182	    if answer is None:
183	        print("No answer to submit through the API (a site submission is entered on the website)", flush=True)
184	        return 0
185	    if not token:
186	        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
187	        return 0
188	    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
189	    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
190	    return 0 if status == 202 else 1
191	
192	
193	if __name__ == "__main__":
194	    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

The agent system, in four steps, each a model at work (the hosted Qwen through the run's proxy):

import asyncio
import json
import re
import sys

SAFETY_S = 60                # an answer after expires_at scores 0


def site(task: dict, site_id: str) -> dict:
    found = next(s for s in task["access"] if s.get("siteId") == site_id)
    return {"url": found["url"], **(found.get("credentials") or {})}


def fill(template: str, **values) -> str:
    text = (PROMPTS / template).read_text()
    for key, value in values.items():
        text = text.replace("{" + key + "}", str(value))
    return text


def site_task(name: str, task: dict, **extra) -> str:
    s = site(task, SITE_IDS[name])
    return fill(f"{name}.md", SITE_URL=s["url"], USERNAME=s.get("username", ""), PASSWORD=s.get("password", ""),
                BRIEF=task["brief"], **extra)


def submission_section(brief: str) -> str:
    """The brief's part about entering the bid (from its "Submission" heading); the whole brief if it has none."""
    match = re.search(r"^#+ *(Submission|Abgabe|Angebotsabgabe)\b.*$", brief, re.M | re.I)
    return brief[match.start():] if match else brief


def german(value) -> str:
    """1234.5 -> "1.234,50", the format the tender portal expects."""
    return f"{Decimal(str(value)):,.2f}".replace(",", "X").replace(".", ",").replace("X", ".")


def bid_text(answer: dict) -> str:
    lines = [f"Tender reference: {answer['tender_reference']}", f"Decision: {answer['decision']}",
             f"Discount: {german(answer['discount_percent'])} %"]
    for p in answer["positions"]:
        lines.append(f"- Position {p['position']}: material {p['material_number']}, quantity {p['quantity']} Stück, "
                     f"unit price {german(p['unit_price'])} EUR, lead time {p['lead_time_weeks']} weeks, "
                     f"base unit price {german(p['base_unit_price'])}, surcharge per unit "
                     f"{german(p['surcharge_per_unit'])}, packaging per unit {german(p['packaging_per_unit'])}, "
                     f"rebate total {german(p['rebate_total'])}")
    lines.append(f"Total net: {german(answer['total_net'])} EUR")
    return "\n".join(lines)


async def research(task: dict, urls: dict, workdir: Path, deadline: float) -> dict:
    """Tender, specification and mailbox in parallel; the ERP as soon as the specification agent has saved the
    requirements with their catalogue groups. Each site gets its own share of the clock."""
    system = (PROMPTS / "system.md").read_text()
    agents: dict[str, Agent] = {}
    start = time.monotonic()

    async def run_site(name: str, prompt: str, until: float) -> dict:
        try:
            async with Agent(name, {name: urls[name]}, workdir) as agent:
                agents[name] = agent
                return await agent.run(system, prompt, min(until, deadline), required=REQUIRED[name])
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001  one site failing must not stop the others
            print(f"[{name}] failed: {error!r}", flush=True)
            return {"name": name, "facts": agents[name].facts if name in agents else None, "error": repr(error)}

    share = deadline - start
    tender = asyncio.create_task(run_site("tender", site_task("tender", task), start + 0.6 * share))
    spec = asyncio.create_task(run_site("spec", site_task("spec", task), start + 0.5 * share))
    mail = asyncio.create_task(run_site("mail", site_task("mail", task), start + 0.75 * share))

    def facts_of(name: str):
        return agents[name].facts if name in agents else None

    async def erp_when_requirements_known():
        while not spec.done() and time.monotonic() < deadline - 0.4 * share:
            f = facts_of("spec")
            if isinstance(f, dict) and f.get("requirements") and "atalog" in json.dumps(f, ensure_ascii=False):
                break
            await asyncio.sleep(5)
        print(f"[erp] starting at {time.monotonic() - start:.0f}s", flush=True)
        requirements = {"specification": facts_of("spec"), "tender": facts_of("tender")}
        return await run_site("erp", site_task("erp", task, REQUIREMENTS=json.dumps(requirements, ensure_ascii=False)),
                              deadline)

    erp = asyncio.create_task(erp_when_requirements_known())
    reports = await asyncio.gather(tender, spec, mail, erp)
    for r in reports:
        print(f"[{r['name']}] {r.get('seconds')}s, usage {r.get('usage')}, summary: {str(r.get('summary'))[:300]}",
              flush=True)
    return {r["name"]: r.get("facts") for r in reports}


async def submit(task: dict, urls: dict, workdir: Path, answer: dict, deadline: float) -> dict:
    t, m = site(task, "tender-portal"), site(task, "mail")
    prompt = fill("submit.md", TENDER_URL=t["url"], TENDER_USERNAME=t.get("username", ""),
                  TENDER_PASSWORD=t.get("password", ""), MAIL_URL=m["url"], MAIL_USERNAME=m.get("username", ""),
                  MAIL_PASSWORD=m.get("password", ""), BRIEF=submission_section(task["brief"]), BID=bid_text(answer))
    system = (PROMPTS / "system.md").read_text()
    async with Agent("submit", {"tender": urls["tender"], "mail": urls["mail"]}, workdir) as agent:
        return await agent.run(system, prompt, deadline, max_turns=120, required=REQUIRED["submit"],
                               progress_checks=False)


async def solve(task: dict, cdp_urls: list[str]) -> dict | None:
    """Research, analyse, price, submit. `task` is the run; `cdp_urls` its browsers, one per website.

    The answer goes on the tender portal ("site" submission), so this returns None; it prints the bid."""
    start = time.monotonic()
    end = start + min(contract.seconds_left(task), 20 * 60) - SAFETY_S
    urls = dict(zip(BROWSERS, cdp_urls))
    workdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rfq-run-"))
    print(f"Workdir {workdir}; {end - start:.0f}s on the clock", flush=True)

    facts = await research(task, urls, workdir, deadline=end - SUBMIT_S - ANALYST_S)
    (workdir / "facts.json").write_text(json.dumps(facts, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
    print(f"Research done at {time.monotonic() - start:.0f}s", flush=True)

    try:
        decided = await analyst.analyse(task["brief"], facts,
                                        timeout=max(60, min(ANALYST_S, end - time.monotonic() - SUBMIT_S)))
        (workdir / "order.json").write_text(json.dumps(decided, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
        positions = (facts.get("tender") or {}).get("positions") if isinstance(facts.get("tender"), dict) else None
        answer = analyst.to_answer(decided, expected_positions=len(positions) if positions else None)
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"Analysis failed: {error!r}", flush=True)
        return None
    print(f"Bid at {time.monotonic() - start:.0f}s: {decided.get('decision')} because {decided.get('decision_notes')}",
          flush=True)
    for line in decided.get("lines") or []:
        print(f"  {line.get('position')}: {line.get('quantity_pieces')} pcs, material {line.get('material')} "
              f"({str(line.get('material_reasoning'))[:200]})", flush=True)
    print(bid_text(answer), flush=True)
    (workdir / "bid.json").write_text(json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))

    report = await submit(task, urls, workdir, answer, deadline=end)
    print(f"Submit: {time.monotonic() - start:.0f}s, usage {report.get('usage')}, facts {report.get('facts')}, "
          f"summary: {report.get('summary')}", flush=True)
    return None


async def main() -> int:
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{s.get('siteId')} {s.get('url')}" for s in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        cdp_urls, local_browsers = await browsers.cdp_endpoints(playwright, len(BROWSERS))
        try:
            answer = await solve(task, cdp_urls)
        finally:
            for browser in local_browsers:
                await browser.close()
    if answer is None:
        print("No answer to submit through the API (a site submission is entered on the website)", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

content.text:
Yes, at its core. `llm_agent.py` (about 290 lines) is a loop that calls Qwen's OpenAI-compatible chat API over and over, runs whatever tools the model asks for, and appends the results to the conversation. `agent.py` arranges several of those loops into a pipeline.

## One agent: the loop (`llm_agent.py`)

```
messages = [system prompt, site task]
loop up to 80 turns, until finish or the deadline:
    response = qwen.chat.completions.create(messages, tools)   # one API call
    for each tool call in the response:
        run it → append the result to messages
```

**Tools the model gets:**
- **Browser tools.** Each agent starts its own **Playwright MCP** server process, attached over CDP to one sandbox browser. The harness offers 14 of its tools, such as `browser_click`, `browser_navigate`, `browser_snapshot` and `browser_evaluate`, named with the browser in front (e.g. `tender__browser_click`). Results come back as a text snapshot of the page, with element refs like `e42`.
- **Three local tools.** `save_facts` writes a JSON object to disk, `read_file` reads downloaded ZIP, PDF or CSV files, and `finish` stops the agent.

**What it adds on top of a bare loop:**
- **Deadlines.** A hard stop, plus a "less than a minute left, save now" message (`llm_agent.py:129`).
- **Required facts.** `finish` is refused while required keys are missing. Once they're all saved, `save_facts` answers "finish now" (`llm_agent.py:181-190`).
- **A progress check every 10 turns** that asks the agent to save.
- **Context compaction.** The latest 2 page snapshots stay whole and older ones are cut to 600 characters (`llm_agent.py:273`).

## The pipeline (`agent.py`)

1. **Research** (`agent.py:79`). The tender, spec and mail agents start in parallel, each on its own browser. The ERP agent waits until the spec agent has saved requirements that name catalogue groups.
2. **Analyst** (`analyst.py`). One Qwen call gets all the facts plus the brief. It returns a structured order: quantities, material, price conditions and discount scope per position, with reasoning.
3. **Pricing** (`pricing.py`). Plain Python, no model: it does the rule arithmetic in `Decimal` with HALF_UP rounding.
4. **Submit** (`agent.py:122`). One more agent drives two browsers, the tender portal and the mail. It enters the bid, gets the TAN from the mail and signs.

The pipeline runs on a fixed time budget: 120 s for the analyst, 570 s for submit and 60 s of safety margin, and research gets whatever is left of the 20 minutes.

## How the code connects to run #1's problems

- **Context is still large even though compaction exists.** It only shortens page snapshots. `browser_evaluate` and `read_file` results stay whole on purpose (up to 14,000 characters each), and in run #1 the agents used evaluate heavily: `innerHTML` dumps and fetch loops over many messages. That's most of the roughly 21K tokens per call.
- **Qwen's thinking isn't limited anywhere.** The API call (`llm_agent.py:139`) only sets `temperature=0.2`, which explains the 100-second calls.
- **Tool calls run one after another.** When the model asks for several in one turn, they run one by one.
- **The ERP agent is gated behind the spec agent.** That's the "ERP got only 2 minutes" problem in run #1.

So it's a plain, readable harness. The weak spots are a few specific settings and the ERP's wait for the spec agent, not the overall design.

content.text:
Yes, and there's a better reason for it than elegance: **the private dataset.** The brief says the final run uses "different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names)" with "the information split differently across them". Your current harness assumes this exact public setup in several places:

- **Four site-specific prompts** (`prompts/tender.md`, `spec.md`, `erp.md`, `mail.md`) with step lists written for these sites.
- **Fixed site IDs** in `SITE_IDS` (`agent.py:29`). `site()` uses `next()` with no default, so a renamed `siteId` would crash the run immediately with `StopIteration`.
- **A fixed dependency:** ERP waits for the spec agent to save "catalog" groups. If the private data puts the catalogue group somewhere else, ERP waits until 40% of the research time is gone.
- **Required keys per site** (`REQUIRED`) that assume which site holds which facts.

An orchestrator that reads the brief and the site list and decides what to research where handles a reshuffled dataset much better.

## How I'd build it: model decides, code guards

**Orchestrator agent** (no browser, small context):
- Reads the brief, the rules and the list of sites from `access`.
- Tools:
  - `start_agent(site, question)`: starts a sub-agent on a free browser and returns an id. It doesn't block, so 4 can run in parallel.
  - `wait_agents()`: returns the facts sub-agents have finished with.
  - `compute_bid(order)`: calls `pricing.py`, so the arithmetic stays in code.
  - `submit(bid)`: starts the submit agent.
- It follows up on what comes back. For example: "spec says Kataloggruppe GR-8923 → start the ERP agent on that". Or: "mail facts lack the Konditionsregeln → send another agent with that question".

**Sub-agents:** your existing `Agent` loop, unchanged, but with **one generic prompt** ("here is the brief, your site and your question") instead of four site scripts.

**Kept in code, not left to the model:**
- at most 4 sub-agents at once, one per browser
- a hard deadline per sub-agent
- a fixed slot reserved for submit
- the pricing arithmetic

The orchestrator decides *what* to do; code guarantees the run finishes and submits.

**Depth:** one level is enough. Deeper recursion (sub-agents spawning their own) adds model calls and latency, and you only have 4 browsers anyway.

## Trade-offs

| | Fixed pipeline (now) | Orchestrator |
|---|---|---|
| Private dataset | brittle | adapts |
| Speed | no planning overhead | +10–20 orchestrator calls, but they're small, and dispatch follows the data instead of fixed waits |
| Reliability | predictable | depends on how well Qwen plans |
| Fair-play review / "elegance" | fine | clearly "model decides" |

The main risk is Qwen as the planner. If it plans badly, the orchestrator is a good place for a stronger model: about 10–20 calls with a small context, so it barely moves the cost score.

**Recommendation:** do it. It also makes most of the earlier speed fixes easier: no gated ERP start, and stopping and follow-ups are decided by the orchestrator. But the other thread is still editing `my-agent/`, so it should be one coordinated change there, not a second rewrite in parallel. Should I write the design as a short spec you can hand to that thread, or build it myself once that thread's test run is done?

Right, Claude Code's Task tool already does this — main agent orchestrating parallel subagents, with background agents too, so this orchestrator design is conceptually the same pattern. content.text:
Yes. What I described is essentially Claude Code's own model: a main agent that hands work to **subagents** through its Agent tool, runs several in parallel and gets back compact results. You wouldn't have to build any of that if Claude Code is your runtime.

**What maps onto Claude Code directly:**
- Orchestrator → Claude Code's main agent.
- `start_agent` / `wait_agents` → its Agent tool. Subagents run in parallel and in their own context, and return only their result.
- Generic site agent → a subagent definition, made from a prompt plus allowed tools. This works with `claude -p --agents '{...}'` or with `agents=` in the Agent SDK.
- Browser tools → 4 Playwright MCP servers in the MCP config, one per sandbox CDP URL.

**What Claude Code doesn't give you, and you'd still add:**
1. **Wall-clock deadlines.** Claude Code has no idea a run has 20 minutes. With the Agent SDK, your Python wrapper keeps the clock: it interrupts sessions, uses hooks to inject "X minutes left, wrap up", and reserves the submit slot.
2. **One browser per subagent.** Two parallel subagents on the same browser would get in each other's way. You'd define 4 subagents, each limited to one browser's MCP tools. A hook can block the orchestrator from starting a second agent on a busy browser; a prompt rule alone isn't a guarantee.
3. **Pricing in code.** Either `pricing.py` becomes an in-process tool, or it runs after the agent finishes.
4. **Locking it down for fair play.** Turn off `Bash`, file editing and web tools so the reviewer only sees browser tools plus your own.

**So the question comes back to the model:**
- **Claude as the model:** use Claude Code or the Agent SDK with subagents and the 4 guardrails above. You get the orchestrator for free and a model that plans well. The cost is higher per run.
- **Staying on Qwen:** Claude Code would need a translation proxy, and its prompts are tuned for Claude. Here a slim orchestrator in your own harness is the better fit, roughly 100 lines on top of the existing `Agent` class.

**Testing it is cheap now.** The plain `claude` CLI supports subagents (`--agents`) and MCP configs (`--mcp-config`), so I could test a Claude Code orchestrator locally on **your subscription**:
- 4 browser-bound subagents against the scouting sites
- research only, without submitting
- measure wall time, turns, tokens and fact completeness against run #1's research phase

That would show directly whether Claude Code with Claude beats your Qwen pipeline on speed and quality. Should I build that in a separate `experiments/` folder?

content.text:
Yes, that's a good design, and it's closer to what you already have than it looks. Today `analyst.py` already outputs a structured order and `pricing.py` already does the arithmetic. Your proposal moves the **rule decisions** from the model into Python as well, and makes the retrieval JSON the single contract between them.

## Why it fits this challenge

- **The rules don't change in the final run.** The private dataset has "the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format". Only the websites and data change. So a rule engine written once in Python carries over to the private dataset, and only retrieval has to adapt.
- **Rules 12–28 are where a model makes mistakes:** withdrawn answers, scoped amendments, shared stock, conditional discount thresholds, cent allocation with largest remainders, HALF_UP at exactly the right step. Python gets these right every time and runs in milliseconds.
- **It's testable.** You can unit-test the engine with made-up fixtures, without a browser.
- **It's faster.** The 190-second analyst call disappears.

## The key design choice: the JSON holds evidence, not conclusions

Retrieval should record **every candidate record**, not the agent's choice. For example: all revisions with their status, all Q&A answers, all director approvals including superseded and other-tender ones, all ERP candidates in the catalogue group. Each record needs the fields the rules sort and filter on: date, exact reference, sender, revision, validity window.

Roughly:

- **tender:** reference, scenario date, positions (id, quantity, unit), and Q&A items. Each Q&A item has a number, date, type (quantity change, withdrawal, technical amendment, Konditionsgruppe, packaging tariff, delivery commitment, setup pool), target position and its values.
- **spec:**
  - revisions (id, status, date)
  - requirements per position: bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification, a "nutzbarer Weg" flag, Kataloggruppe, pieces per set
- **erp:** candidate materials, each with:
  - status and attributes
  - stock, stock and production lead times
  - carton size, allocation mass, surcharge mass, setup fee
  - price conditions: validity, scales, currency, price unit, FX key
- **mail:** messages with id, folder, sender, date, subject and reference, plus their parsed content: approval % and minimum order value, Konditionsregeln, metal index windows, FX rates, packaging tariffs, delivery commitments, setup pool fee, bonus bands, Technikfreigabe reserve.

Python then applies the rules: latest record for the exact reference up to the scenario date, withdrawals, amendments, exact material match, scale prices, shared stock, discount threshold, and so on.

**Where the model still has to interpret prose:** the Konditionsregeln text ("does the discount apply to base only, base plus surcharge, or neither"), the cent-allocation rule in the Rüstpools mail, and the bonus bands. The schema should make these **enums or numbers the extraction agent fills in**, so the engine never parses German text.

## Two additions I'd make

1. **Gap check, then follow-up.** Python can detect holes in milliseconds: a position without a requirement, a material without a price condition valid on the scenario date, a Konditionsgruppe key with no matching rules mail. It turns them into targeted questions for the retrieval agent while time is left. That's much faster than agents re-checking everything on their own.
2. **Fair-play safeguard.** The rules say the model "makes the decisions" and chooses "what matters", while code may do "parsing, arithmetic, checks". The extraction agent deciding what's relevant (this mail is a director approval for our tender; this answer withdraws #8153) covers "what matters". Python sorting by date and computing prices counts as rule-checking and arithmetic. To be safe, the agent should also record its own pick (e.g. `governing_approval: MSG-…`), and Python checks it against its own result and writes any disagreement into `notes`. Then a reviewer sees "model decides, code checks", not "code decides".

**Retrieval:** one agent can do it in principle, but splitting the schema by site and filling the sections in parallel with up to 4 browsers costs nothing extra and saves several minutes.

## Next step

The schema is the core of this design. I'd write it as typed Python models (Pydantic) derived from rules 1–28, plus the rule engine and unit tests with made-up fixtures, kept separate from `my-agent/` so it doesn't clash with the other thread. Then retrieval and `analyst.py` get rewired to it. Should I start with the schema?

3	You work in sales engineering for Linden Hydraulik und Komponenten GmbH, a German hydraulics and components manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). The scenario date is 2027-01-25T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2027-02-12T11:00:00Z.
4	
5	Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.
6	
7	## Rules
8	
9	1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
10	2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
11	3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
12	4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
13	5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
14	6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
15	7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
16	8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.
17	
18	
19	## Additional rules
20	
21	These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.
22	
23	- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
24	- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
25	- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
26	- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
27	- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
28	- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
29	- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
30	- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
31	- Units: tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
32	- Pricing breakdown: base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
33	- These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
34	- Technical derivation: for a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
35	- Authority and time: resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
36	- Currency: the valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
37	- Packaging: Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
38	- Delivery: Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
39	- Shared setup: Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
40	- Project bonus: the finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier).
